public_rationale: At launch, Altman acknowledged missing capabilities needed for AGI, with continuous learning given as a concrete example. OpenAI also documented substantial performance across occupations, but those results did not establish the broad general capability in the stated reading. The claim is supported under that reading, rather than proved under every possible definition of AGI.
limitations: The outcome depends on the stated interpretation of AGI.
The decisive acknowledgment is reported by WIRED.
Neither failing to learn continuously nor any single benchmark is a definition-independent AGI test.

our_interpretation: The claim concerns the GPT-5 system announced on August 7, 2025.
The ordinary reading of AGI is broadly human-level general cognitive capability, including reliable adaptation and learning across unfamiliar tasks.
Strong performance on selected benchmarks or expert-level answers in some domains does not by itself establish AGI.
Obviously expresses confidence; it adds no separate measurable threshold.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence identifies substantial missing general capabilities, supported by evaluations or a concrete acknowledgment from the developer that the launched system falls short of AGI.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, credible evaluations establish general human-level capability and adaptation across unfamiliar intellectual tasks, rather than isolated benchmark successes.
